root_cause: Application debug logging (LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG, SQL_QUERY_LOGGING=true) was left enabled after deployment of checkout-api v2.14.3 on Jan 14. Verbose SQL query logging generated ~50GB/hr, filling the 500GB /var/log partition in approximately 9 hours.

timeline.event: Deployment of checkout-api v2.14.3 with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG and SQL_QUERY_LOGGING=true
Disk usage at 42% - normal growth rate not yet alarming
Disk usage reached 90% - warning threshold hit
Log rotation failed - checkout-api.log too large (48GB)
First write failure: 'No space left on device'
Nginx error log writes failing, buffering in memory
Checkout API returning 500 errors - cannot create temp files
PagerDuty incident created: checkout API 500 errors
OOM kill of checkout-api process, restart fails due to no disk space

evidence: Deploy log shows LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG and SQL_QUERY_LOGGING=true enabled at 18:00:15
Log rotation failed at 00:05 because checkout-api.log was 48GB (exceeds maxsize)
First 'No space left on device' error at 03:10:15
Checkout API restart failed at 03:25:35 - cannot write PID file
contributing_factors: No log rotation size limit configured for the debug log file
Disk usage alerting only triggered at 90% - no earlier warning thresholds
Deployment pipeline has no validation for production log levels
Health checks did not verify disk space as a dependency
